title: Truncation error for sign-valued trees
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let $T$ be a decision tree on $A$ with real outputs. Suppose $T(x)\in\{-1,1\}$ for every input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. For every natural number $k$, the expected squared difference between $T(x)$ and the tree obtained by truncating $T$ at depth $k$ and assigning $0$ at truncated leaves is at most the number of leaves of $T$ multiplied by $2^{-k}$.
hypotheses_covered: A set of available coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
A real-valued decision tree on that set
